respondent:
State of Rajasthan
Supreme Court of India

8 January 2003
Appeal (Cr.) 1150-1151 of 2001, Appeal (Cr.) 42-43 of 2002
The Judgment was delivered by : B. P. Singh, J.
1.  These appeals by special leave have been preferred by Chittarmal and Moti who have impugned the judgment and order of the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan, Jaipur Bench, Jaipur in DB Crl. Appeal No.563 of 1997 and DB Cr. (Jail) Appeal No. 1 of 1998 dated 5th September, 2000. The High Court while acquitting the other accused of the charges levelled against them, found the appellants guilty of the offences punishable u/ss. 302 and 307 IPC. The appellants who had been sentenced to death by the trial court for committing the offence punishable u/s. 302 IPC, were sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life declining the death reference. The trial court had also sentenced the appellants to undergo five years rigorous imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.2000/ for the offence punishable u/s. 307 IPC
facts: The case of the prosecution is that on the night intervening 27th 28th April, 1989 deceased Bhura and Ram Narain and Lal Chand, PW.1 were sleeping in their house in village Joshian Ki Dhani when the appellants herein alongwith five other persons entered the house at about 10 or 11 p.m. and brutally assaulted Bhura and Ram Narain as also Lal Chand, PW.1.

The first information report Ex.P.1 was lodged by Bhenru, PW.5 another son of Bhura (deceased) alleging that on the night of occurrence Moti (appellant) alongwith Ramsi, Ratan, Lala, Chhagan, Jaggu and 2 3 others armed with axes, farsies and swords entered the house of Bhura and mounted a murderous assault as a result of which Bhura and Ram Narain lost their lives while Lal Chand, PW.1 was severely injured.

The trial court had also sentenced the appellants to undergo five years rigorous imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs.2000/ for the offence punishable u/s. 307 IPC, in default of payment of fine, six months simple imprisonment, which was upheld by the High Court.
issues: Whether the appellants were guilty of the offences punishable under sections 302 and 307 IPC?
Whether the trial court's finding that all the accused were guilty of the offence punishable under section 148 IPC was correct?
court_reasoning: The High Court did not accept the claim of Bhenru, PW.5 of being an eye witness.

The High Court noticed the evidence of the other witnesses and finding considerable inconsistency in the testimony of the witnesses came to the conclusion that neither Bhenru nor those witnesses had witnessed the occurrence.
The High Court found that so far as Lal Chand, PW.1 was concerned, his presence at the place of occurrence could not be disputed.
Lal Chand's evidence cannot be discarded on the grounds urged by the defence.
holding: The appellants were found guilty of the offences punishable under sections 302 and 307 IPC.
The conviction of the appellants u/s. 148 IPC was set aside.
